# Vertical overlay: Manufacturing

**Level:** NAICS 2022 sector 31-33 (parent vertical)
**CISA critical infrastructure sectors nested here:** Chemical, Critical Manufacturing, Defense Industrial Base
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 334510 Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing. Connected medical device manufacturer (electromedical equipment).
**Primary system:** Device software development and manufacturing systems (PLM and MES)

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
Department of Defense (DFARS/CMMC, DCSA); Department of State DDTC (ITAR); Department of Commerce BIS (EAR, ICTS); FDA (medical device cybersecurity, food facilities); CISA (Chemical & Critical Manufacturing SRMA)

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**FD&C Act section 524B (cyber devices)**, 21 U.S.C. 360n-2. Cris Santos Company's primary industry here is connected medical devices, and section 524B is binding on every premarket submission for a cyber device (vulnerability monitoring and disclosure plan, secure development, patching, SBOM). Research note: for defense suppliers the better target is NIST SP 800-171 via DFARS 252.204-7012 and CMMC (see the Defense Industrial Base child); for other manufacturers with no binding rule, benchmark against NIST CSF 2.0 and NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3.
Source: https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title21-section360n-2&num=0&edition=prelim

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** Device design files and source code; SBOMs and vulnerability data; export-controlled technical data (EAR/ITAR where applicable); patient data received from devices in service (may be PHI when handled for a covered entity)
- **Critical systems:** MES; ERP / PLM; DCS / PLCs / robotics; SCADA and historians; Quality/LIMS; CAD/CAM and CNC networks
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** None identified beyond cross-sector obligations
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** None noted
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Exploited vulnerability in a fielded connected medical device
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** AI-enabled device software function (image analysis)

## Notes
FAR CUI proposed rule (FR 2024-30437, Jan. 15, 2025) not yet final; FAR is being rewritten under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (2026 proposed rules). NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 exists but CMMC and DoD assessments remain tied to Rev. 2. SEC cross-cutting note in n11.
